name: Terracotta Army of Qin Shi Huang
description: Subterranean army of 8,000 unique life-sized soldiers, acclaimed as the 'Eighth Wonder of the World'.
history: Constructed to guard the first Emperor of unified China, Qin Shi Huang, in the afterlife. Discovered by local farmers in Lintong District, Xi'an in 1974.
construction: Over 700,000 workers molded and fired individual terracotta figures, each with distinct facial features, hairstyles, armor, and bronze weaponry.
architecture: Massive four-pit subterranean necropolis covering over 56 square kilometers, originally painted in vibrant cinnabar, malachite, and azurite pigments.
significance: Acclaimed worldwide as the 'Eighth Wonder of the World' following French Prime Minister Jacques Chirac's declaration in 1978; UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987.
currentStatus: Excavated and displayed in the Emperor Qinshihuang's Mausoleum Site Museum.
wonderCategory: Eighth Wonder of the World (International Acclaim)
wonderHistoricalContext: In 1978, during an official state visit, French statesman Jacques Chirac declared: 'There were Seven Wonders in the world, and the discovery of the Terracotta Army is the Eighth.' It remains universally recognized under this title.
